content:
Sam: Quick design question — for the new scoring endpoint should we return raw logits, normalized 0-1 scores, or both? thinking about routing, quota units, and dashboard UX.
Anita: My vote is both. raw logits for downstream flexibility, normalized for easy thresholding in the console.
Leo: +1 for both but we need a single canonical unit for billing/quotas. otherwise consoles/alerts will be confusing.
Maya: what do folks think about counting quota by candidates vs calls? e.g. 1 request with 100 candidates vs 10 requests with 10 candidates.
Chris: we currently meter tokens and calls. for reranking we should probably meter candidate evaluation units. suggest name: `candidate_units`.
Anita: `candidate_units` sounds good. mapping: cost = sum(num_candidates * model_cost_per_candidate). simple and explainable.
Sam: ok — how do we expose that in the response? do we include `units_used`? do we put a header `X-Candidate-Units`?
Leo: both. header for quick gateway accounting, field in body for audits/evals.
Maya: also need to standardize score semantics for routing policies. e.g. some routing rules expect higher-is-better normalized [0,1]. if we expose both we need clear docs on which to use for policy.
Chris: propose this response shape: 
```json
{
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "score": 3.2, "norm_score": 0.87},
    {"id": "c2", "score": -1.1, "norm_score": 0.12}
  ],
  "units_used": 2
}
```
header: `X-Candidate-Units: 2`
Sam: Implementation Q: normalization should be per-request softmax or per-model calibrated scaler? different customers expect different semantics.
Anita: default to softmax over the returned candidates for `norm_score` (interpretable for selection). we can add `calibrated_score` later if needed.
Leo: softmax is fine but call it out explicitly in the contract. also note numerical stability for large logits — the runtime should apply standard log-sum-exp.
Maya: routing implications: our smart-router currently makes choices based on estimated latency and model tier. we should add `expected_candidate_cost` to routing decision: cheaper model for high candidate count.
Chris: agree. route rule example: 
`if num_candidates <= 8 -> prefer-model: fast-small`
`if num_candidates >= 64 -> prefer-model: high-accuracy`
plus a fallback policy `on-oversubscription -> degrade-to: fast-small`
Sam: do we want automatic fallback that reduces candidate set (top-K) or switch model to keep latency SLO?
Anita: prefer model switch. reducing candidate set silently can regress quality unexpectedly. fallback switch + annotated response `fallback_reason` is better.
Leo: and we need telemetry hooks: emit `scorer.fallback` event with fields `{route, original_model, fallback_model, candidates_requested, candidates_returned, latency_ms}`. telemetry-bot link to dashboard.
telemetry-bot: Dashboard draft: https://dash.redwood.local/scorer/overview — shows `median_latency`, `p50_units_per_call`, `fallback_rate`, `per-model_candidate_cost`.
Maya: console UX: add per-route toggle `prefer_cost_over_latency` and preview estimated cost delta for sample requests.
Chris: can we plumb `prefer_model` via header `X-Prefer-Model: model-id` and `X-Prefer-Tier: cost|latency|balanced`? this helps migrations/canaries.
Sam: good idea. authorize header only for internal keys or enterprise plans.
Anita: one more: quota naming. `candidate_units` for billing, expose `scorer_calls` for rate-limit. both should appear in console and billing export.
Leo: add audit tag for canary: `X-Canary-Tag` so we can split telemetry by canary group.
deploy-bot: FYI I'll queue a canary deploy of the router + scoring contract to staging at 10:00 PST. link: https://deploys/redwood/abc123 :rocket:
Maya: test plan: generate 3 workloads: low-cand(5), mid(30), high(200). verify routing + fallback + `units_used` matches expected.
Sam: action items: 1) API contract PR (Anita) 2) router rule extension + header support (Chris) 3) telemetry events + dashboard vars (Leo/Maya) 4) staging canary (deploy-bot). i'll collect PR links in this thread. :thumbsup:
Chris: I'll add a small note in docs about choosing `norm_score` vs `score` in routing rules.
Anita: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/scorer-api/pull/412 — includes JSON schema and examples.
Sam: awesome. meeting? quick 15 to align on edge cases tomorrow.
Maya: yep, 15 works. I'll bring perf numbers for candidate cost.
Sam: thanks team — closing thread after the canary results. :white_check_mark:
